falseSynonyms.zh: - It began to rain. = 下雨開始了。 - It became cold. = 天氣變冷了。
falseSynonyms.point: Trap: begin means “start.” become means “change into a new state.” Compare: Do not use become simply because something changes at the beginning of a process.

falseSynonyms.zh: Trap: To create something is to make it exist. To begin something is to start it. Compare: - They began the project in March. - They created a new software tool. Something can be created and then begin operating later.
falseSynonyms.point: Trap: To create something is to make it exist. To begin something is to start it. Compare: - They began the project in March. - They created a new software tool. Something can be created and then begin operating later.

falseSynonyms.zh: Trap: Preparation happens before the main activity begins. Compare: - We prepared for the meeting at 8:30. - The meeting began at 9:00.
falseSynonyms.point: Trap: Preparation happens before the main activity begins. Compare: - We prepared for the meeting at 8:30. - The meeting began at 9:00.

falseSynonyms.zh: Trap: Introduce can mean present something new, but it does not always mean the activity itself begins. Compare: - The school introduced a new policy. - The policy came into effect in September.
falseSynonyms.point: Trap: Introduce can mean present something new, but it does not always mean the activity itself begins. Compare: - The school introduced a new policy. - The policy came into effect in September.

falseSynonyms.zh: These are opposites in many contexts. - begin = start - continue = keep going after the start
falseSynonyms.point: These are opposites in many contexts. - begin = start - continue = keep going after the start

falseSynonyms.zh: initiate = deliberately cause something to begin. originate = be the source or first point of something. Compare: - The manager initiated the review. - The idea originated in the design team.
falseSynonyms.point: initiate = deliberately cause something to begin. originate = be the source or first point of something. Compare: - The manager initiated the review. - The idea originated in the design team.

falseSynonyms.zh: Both may mean “begin,” but launch usually implies a planned, organized, and often public beginning. - start a car - start work - launch a product - launch a campaign “Launch the car” normally means physically send it forward or introduce a model, not simply turn on the engine.
falseSynonyms.point: Both may mean “begin,” but launch usually implies a planned, organized, and often public beginning. - start a car - start work - launch a product - launch a campaign “Launch the car” normally means physically send it forward or introduce a model, not simply turn on the engine.

falseSynonyms.zh: These are different verbs. - arise = appear / come into existence - raise = lift something or cause something to increase Compare: - A problem arose. - She raised a question. - The company raised prices.
falseSynonyms.point: These are different verbs. - arise = appear / come into existence - raise = lift something or cause something to increase Compare: - A problem arose. - She raised a question. - The company raised prices.

falseSynonyms.zh: emerge often happens gradually or without one clear agent. launch is deliberate. Compare: - New evidence emerged. - Police launched an investigation.
falseSynonyms.point: emerge often happens gradually or without one clear agent. launch is deliberate. Compare: - New evidence emerged. - Police launched an investigation.

falseSynonyms.zh: Both can describe a beginning, but their tone and context are very different. - The conference kicked off at nine. - A fight broke out after the game. Do not say a normal conference “broke out.”
falseSynonyms.point: Both can describe a beginning, but their tone and context are very different. - The conference kicked off at nine. - A fight broke out after the game. Do not say a normal conference “broke out.”

falseSynonyms.zh: set about + noun / -ing = start working on something. set out to + verb = begin with the intention of achieving something. Compare: - She set about writing the report. - She set out to prove the theory wrong.
falseSynonyms.point: set about + noun / -ing = start working on something. set out to + verb = begin with the intention of achieving something. Compare: - She set about writing the report. - She set out to prove the theory wrong.

falseSynonyms.zh: start is very broad. take up is especially natural when beginning a hobby, activity, subject, or role. - start exercising - take up yoga - take up painting - take up a new post Both can be followed by: - noun - begin the lesson - start the lesson - to-infinitive - begin to speak - start to speak - -ing - begin speaking - start speaking In many contexts, begin to do and begin doing are both correct. Example: - It began to rain. - It began raining. Both are natural. Often followed by a noun: - commence work - commence proceedings - commence operations It can also be intransitive: - The ceremony commenced at noon. Usually takes an object: - initiate a review - initiate contact - initiate proceedings Not usually: - “The review initiated.” ✗ Better: - The review began. - The committee initiated the review. Pattern: embark on + noun / noun phrase - embark on a journey - embark on a project - embark on a career Not: - embark to study ✗ Better: - embark on a course of study - begin to study Pattern: set about + noun / -ing - set about the task - set about solving the problem Pattern: set out to + base verb - set out to improve - set out to investigate - set out to build Usually no object: - The project got underway. - The talks got underway. Not: - “They got underway the project.” ✗ Intransitive: - a problem arises - difficulties arise No direct object. Pattern: take up + noun / -ing-like activity noun - take up tennis - take up painting - take up a position
falseSynonyms.point: start is very broad. take up is especially natural when beginning a hobby, activity, subject, or role. - start exercising - take up yoga - take up painting - take up a new post Both can be followed by: - noun - begin the lesson - start the lesson - to-infinitive - begin to speak - start to speak - -ing - begin speaking - start speaking In many contexts, begin to do and begin doing are both correct. Example: - It began to rain. - It began raining. Both are natural. Often followed by a noun: - commence work - commence proceedings - commence operations It can also be intransitive: - The ceremony commenced at noon. Usually takes an object: - initiate a review - initiate contact - initiate proceedings Not usually: - “The review initiated.” ✗ Better: - The review began. - The committee initiated the review. Pattern: embark on + noun / noun phrase - embark on a journey - embark on a project - embark on a career Not: - embark to study ✗ Better: - embark on a course of study - begin to study Pattern: set about + noun / -ing - set about the task - set about solving the problem Pattern: set out to + base verb - set out to improve - set out to investigate - set out to build Usually no object: - The project got underway. - The talks got underway. Not: - “They got underway the project.” ✗ Intransitive: - a problem arises - difficulties arise No direct object. Pattern: take up + noun / -ing-like activity noun - take up tennis - take up painting - take up a position
